title: Build the Shortest Bridge

concept.title: Flood one island, then grow it layer by layer until it touches the other
body: The map has exactly **two islands**. You may change water cells into land. What is the smallest number of water cells you must change to connect the two islands with a land path? It is the length (counted in water cells) of the **shortest path over water** from one island to the other.

Do it in two steps. **Step 1:** find one land cell, flood-fill its island, and remember all its cells. **Step 2:** run a breadth-first search **starting from all cells of that island at once**, spreading over water layer by layer. Each layer adds one more row of water cells to the bridge. When the search first touches a land cell that is **not** in the first island, it has reached the second island; the number of the layer tells how many water cells the bridge needed.
This idea, "flood the first object, then grow it with a BFS until the second object is found", is the way to find the **shortest distance between two groups**. The time is O(h * w).

statement: A grid of `h` rows and `w` columns has land (`1`) and water (`0`). It contains exactly two islands, where an island is a group of land cells connected through their sides. You may turn water cells into land. Print the smallest number of water cells that must be turned into land so that the two islands become one island.
inputFormat: The first line has `h` and `w`: the number of rows and columns.
Each of the next `h` lines has a row of `w` characters.
constraints: The grid has exactly two islands (groups of land cells connected through their sides).

examples.note: The islands are the cell (1, 2) and the cell (3, 3). Turning the cells (2, 2) and (2, 3) into land joins them: 2.

hints: Find one land cell and flood its island; remember its cells.
Run a breadth-first search from all these cells at once, through water cells, one layer at a time.
The first land cell that is not in the first island ends the search; the number of completed layers is the answer.

solution.complexity: Time O(h * w), space O(h * w).
